name: Send yourself a weekly digest of unanswered quotes with Gmail and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## The quotes you forgot to chase — in your inbox every Monday

### How it works
Every Monday morning this workflow reads your quotes sheet, finds every quote still marked `open`, and works out how long each one has been sitting without an answer. It sorts them by money at risk and emails you one short digest: what is going cold, what needs a nudge this week, and what is still fresh. **Nothing is ever sent to your customers** — this is a report for you.

It also writes one row per week into a small log sheet, so after a month you can see whether your pipeline is drying up or piling up. That same log is what stops a second digest going out if you re-run the workflow by hand.

### Setup
1. Connect **Gmail** and **Google Sheets** (one-click Google sign-in on n8n Cloud).
2. Quotes sheet headers: `quote_id, customer_name, quote_amount, sent_date, status` — set `status` to `open`, `won` or `lost`, and write `sent_date` as YYYY-MM-DD.
3. Log sheet headers: `week_start, open_count, value_at_risk, needs_nudge, going_cold, sent_at`. Leave the rows empty; the workflow fills them.
4. Select your sheets in all three Google Sheets nodes, and put your own email address and the two day thresholds in **⚙️ Your settings**. Heads-up: picking a sheet in **Log this week's snapshot** silently resets that node's column settings - re-open it and restore Map Automatically, match on week_start, Cell Format = Let n8n format.
5. Open **Workflow settings → Timezone** and pick your own. Both the Monday 8am send and the day counts follow it. Then activate.

## 1. Read what you already track
Runs every Monday at 8am. Pulls your quotes sheet and the small digest log. Both reads always output data, so the very first run still works while the log sheet is still empty.

## 2. Work out what is stalling
Keeps the quotes marked `open`, counts days since `sent_date` in your workflow timezone, sorts by money at risk, and buckets them into going cold, needs a nudge, still fresh. Stops here if this week's digest already went out.

## 3. Mail it, then log it
Sends one HTML digest to your own inbox — never to a customer — then writes one row for the week into the log sheet. Re-run it the same week and it stops before sending: that week is already logged.
